_comment: AI neural network and PPO hyperparameters. All tunable constants live here, not hardcoded - mirrors physics.json/attributes.json pattern.

logging._comment_consistency_interval_s: How often the match logger emits a 'consistency' snapshot entry when no other events have fired (seconds of sim time).

eval._comment: Seeded evaluation, shared by PPOTrainer._eval_vs_rules() (pre-training + every rollout) and evaluate.py -- see ai/eval/seeded_eval.py. eval_n_seeds fixed scenario seeds starting at eval_seed_base are reused identically every eval call, so results are comparable across an entire run instead of noise from a fresh random scenario draw each time. eval_repeats_per_seed re-runs each seed that many times (averaged into the same aggregate stats) to reduce residual match-physics/PPO-sampling noise without growing the scenario set. eval_n_parallel_workers >1 spawns that many subprocesses (mirrors ppo.n_parallel_envs); this does NOT seed PPO training itself, only evaluation call sites.

observation._comment_max_task_ids: Width of the GlobalFeatures task-id one-hot (scaffolding, see ai/knowledge.md 'Task-id: scaffolded, not yet load-bearing'). Must match schema.py's MAX_TASK_IDS.
observation._comment_sim_dt_s: Physics tick size. Default 0.0333 (30Hz). Increase for faster training: 0.05=20Hz (~1.5x), 0.067=15Hz (~2x). UI ignores this and always uses 30Hz.
observation._comment_time: Use log1p normalization for time_remaining to spread out the low end (see ai_design_doc.md section 7.5)

network._comment_inter_player_attn_heads: Heads for the inter-player self-attention pass that runs over other-player embeddings BEFORE the main query step. Divisors of entity_embed_dim (45): 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. 0 = disabled. No-op in 1v1; becomes useful for 2v2+ where player-player relational context matters.
network._comment_share_entity_encoder: If true, ExecutionNetwork reuses DecisionNetwork's entity_encoder, ball_mlp, and global_mlp (same nn.Module objects, shared weights + shared gradient). Halves encoder computation per decision tick. Set false to give each network fully independent encoders.
network._comment_exec_trunk_hidden: Trunk hidden dim for the main policy ExecutionNetwork. null = fall back to trunk_hidden. Set a smaller int (e.g. 96) to reduce execution network capacity and rely more on the decision latent.
network._comment_value_net_trunk_hidden: Optional override for trunk_hidden used ONLY by the dedicated separate value network (trainer.value_net, see ppo.__init__ 'separate_value_net' / CLI --separate-value-net). null (default) = same size as the main trunk_hidden above. Set an int (e.g. 96 for a smaller/cheaper critic, or 384 for a bigger one) to size the standalone critic's trunk independently of the shared policy trunk -- has NO effect at all when --separate-value-net is not passed (the main execution_net always uses trunk_hidden).
network._comment_value_hidden_dim: Hidden layer size for value_head (critic). 0 = old behaviour, a single Linear(trunk_hidden+value_extra_hidden, 1) with no nonlinearity. >0 inserts one Linear+ReLU hidden layer before the final scalar output, giving the critic its own nonlinear capacity instead of relying purely on a linear readout of the shared (policy) trunk. Try 32-128; raise if value RMSE plateaus well above 0 while train loss for the policy looks fine.
network._comment_value_dropout: Dropout probability applied ONLY inside value_head (ExecutionNetwork), immediately before each Linear layer -- never touches the shared trunk `h` that also feeds the policy/motor heads, so it cannot destabilise action distributions. 0.0 (default) = disabled. Motivated by pretrain_value() overfitting hard on a small offline rollout (train loss falling steadily while val loss rises after ~epoch 4-5, see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'value_head overfitting'). Try 0.1-0.3. Note: nn.Dropout auto-disables under .eval() but PPO rollout action-sampling does NOT call .eval() on execution_net, so this also lightly perturbs the value estimate used for GAE bootstrapping during rollout collection -- harmless (value isn't used to pick actions) but worth knowing if you see val= jitter increase after enabling.
network._comment: Shared-trunk actor/critic (Option A from section 9.4). Switch to separate trunk if value loss destabilises policy.

ppo._comment_gamma: Discount factor: how much future rewards are worth vs immediate ones. Think of it as 'I care about a reward in N steps at gamma^N of its face value'. 0.99 = reward 100 steps away is worth 37% of today's reward. 0.995 = same reward is still worth 61%. Typical range: 0.95–0.999. We use 0.995 because episodes are long (~120s, ~170 decision steps) and the terminal reward (+5) is the main signal — too low and the agent gives up on distant goals, too high and variance explodes. Raise toward 0.999 if the agent seems short-sighted; lower toward 0.99 if training is unstable.
ppo._comment_lam: GAE lambda: controls the bias/variance tradeoff in advantage estimation. lam=1.0 is pure Monte Carlo (low bias, high variance — noisy but unbiased). lam=0.0 is pure TD(0) (high bias, low variance — smooth but wrong). Typical range: 0.9–0.99. We use 0.97 as a standard middle ground. Lower (e.g. 0.9) if gradients are noisy and training oscillates; raise (e.g. 0.99) if the agent seems to discount future steps too aggressively.
ppo._comment_clip_range: PPO clipping: the policy ratio (new_prob / old_prob) is clamped to [1-clip, 1+clip] = [0.95, 1.05] here. This stops a single update from changing the policy too drastically — the gradient is zeroed for any sample where the ratio goes outside the band. Typical value is 0.2; we use 0.05 (very conservative) because the KL was spiking to 0.4+ with 0.1, causing early-stop after just 2 minibatches. Lower clip = more conservative updates, more minibatches get through. If you see 25+ minibatches per rollout and training is slow, try raising to 0.1.
ppo._comment_vf_coef: Value function loss coefficient: scales how hard the critic trains relative to the actor. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy. Typical: 0.5. Raise if the value estimates are wildly off (large RMSE vs returns std); lower if value gradients seem to destabilise the policy (rare).
ppo._comment_ent_coef: Entropy bonus: rewards the policy for being uncertain/exploratory. Higher = more random behaviour, harder to converge to a good strategy but less likely to get stuck in local optima. Typical range: 0.0–0.1. We use 0.1 (fairly high) because the agent needs to explore a large action space and sprint/kick/tackle heads that start at ~50% probability. Lower toward 0.01 later in training once the policy has converged to sensible behaviour.
ppo._comment_max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping: if the total gradient vector has magnitude > this, all gradients are scaled down proportionally. Acts as a safety valve against catastrophic updates from rare high-loss samples. 0.5 is standard for PPO. Raise to 1.0 if gradients feel too constrained (loss barely moves per step); lower to 0.3 if you see sudden policy collapses. Check the 'g=' value in the per-rollout log — if it's consistently hitting 0.5 exactly, you're clipping every update. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std) when direction_max_grad_norm below is set — those get their own isolated clip_grad_norm_() call.
ppo._comment_direction_max_grad_norm: Optional separate gradient-norm clip applied ONLY to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction Linear weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std). null (default) = fall back to max_grad_norm, i.e. direction params are clipped together with everything else in one combined-norm group (prior behaviour). Set a float (e.g. 0.05) to isolate direction gradients into their own clip so a single outlier sample's large move_dir/kick_dir gradient can no longer force a proportional shrink of the rest of the network's gradient in the same step (and vice versa — a calm direction gradient no longer 'borrows' clip headroom from a genuinely large gradient elsewhere). See ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'grad norm clipping' discussion for the rationale; this directly bounds how far move_direction's predicted mean can move per gradient step, which is the root cause of the large angular_diff KL outliers seen in training logs.
ppo._comment_learning_rate: Step size for Adam optimiser. Typical PPO LR is 3e-4, but we use 5e-6 because (a) augmentation multiplies the effective batch by 12x meaning each gradient step sees more signal, and (b) the BC-pretrained policy is already near a good point so large steps would destroy it. Raise to 1e-5 if training feels too slow; lower to 1e-6 if the policy collapses after pretraining. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params when direction_learning_rate below is set — those get their own Adam param group/LR.
ppo._comment_direction_learning_rate: Optional separate Adam LR for the direction-head param group (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_std/kick_dir_log_std). null (default) = fall back to learning_rate, i.e. direction params share the main 'policy' param group's LR (prior behaviour). Set a float smaller than learning_rate to directly shrink how much move_direction's predicted mean can move per gradient step, independent of the rest of the policy — complementary to direction_max_grad_norm (LR scales the step size AFTER grad-norm clipping bounds the raw gradient magnitude).
ppo._comment_value_learning_rate: Separate, much higher LR for the value_head (+ value_extra_mlp) param group only — the policy LR above is deliberately tiny to protect the BC-primed policy, but sharing it with the critic starves value learning: the per-minibatch KL early-stop (see target_kl) is based on policy KL and often cuts a rollout's gradient steps to 1-5, which was leaving the value head unable to track the shifting self-play return distribution (normalized value loss stuck >1.0 post-PPO despite a well-converged pretrain). Comparable in scale to value_pretrain_lr/demo_value_pretrain_lr. Falls back to `learning_rate` if absent.
ppo._comment_value_weight_decay: Adam weight_decay (L2) applied ONLY to the value param group ('value_head'/'value_ai_type_channel' params, or trainer.value_net's optimizer when --separate-value-net) during PPO. 0.0 (default) = disabled, matching prior behaviour. Each rollout's data is used for only ppo.n_epochs passes and the return distribution keeps shifting under self-play, so overfitting-to-one-batch is less of a risk here than in bc.value_pretrain_weight_decay's offline setting -- this is mainly cheap insurance for generalisation across the whole run. Try 1e-4 to 1e-3.
ppo._comment_value_only_continuation_epochs: Epoch budget for the value-only continuation loop that runs after the policy's per-minibatch KL early-stop cuts the main epoch loop short (see target_kl) — trains ONLY the value_head/value_extra_mlp param group (no policy forward/backward, so no further KL risk) for up to this many additional passes over the same rollout batch. Defaults to n_epochs if absent (previous, implicit behaviour was to reuse n_epochs unconditionally). Raise if 'val=' stays high despite frequent early-stops; lower if you're worried about overfitting the critic to a single stale rollout batch (see ai/knowledge.md).
ppo._comment_target_kl: Per-minibatch early-stop threshold. KL divergence measures how much the policy distribution has changed since the rollout was collected — KL=0 means no change, KL=0.4 means fairly significant shift. When any minibatch's KL exceeds this, the entire epoch loop stops early. Typical value is 0.01–0.05; we use 0.4 (very permissive) because we want to see how many minibatches naturally get through. The real constraint is clip_range=0.05. LOWER this (e.g. 0.1) to make early-stop fire sooner and protect the policy more aggressively — you'll see fewer minibatches per rollout but more stable training. RAISE it if you want to see the full picture of how the policy changes per rollout.
ppo._comment_n_parallel_envs: Number of worker PROCESSES running independent ScenarioEnv copies for on-policy rollout collection. 1 (default) = current single-process behaviour, no subprocess overhead. >1 spawns that many subprocesses (see ai/ppo/rollout_worker.py), each with its own env + local policy copy, weight-synced from the main process before every rollout. Used by BOTH: (1) the main PPO training loop (rollout_steps split evenly across workers), and (2) pretrain_value()'s/pretrain_combined()'s Phase 2/3 value-warm-up rollout collection (its own n_steps split the same way) -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Parallel rollout collection'. Physics stepping is pure-Python/CPU-bound (GIL-limited under threads), so this only helps via real OS processes. Does NOT affect BC pre-training's dataset epochs or the PPO/value gradient updates themselves -- those stay single-process.
ppo._comment_worker_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() inside each rollout worker process (see n_parallel_envs). Each worker only ever does batch-of-1 CPU forward passes, so >1 thread just adds intra-process contention across N worker processes competing for the same cores; 1 (default) is correct almost always.
ppo._comment_main_process_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() in the main process for train.py and debug_value_network.py -- BC pre-training and the PPO/value gradient update run small-batch ops here, unrelated to worker_torch_threads/n_parallel_envs above. Unlike batch-of-1 rollout workers, PyTorch's all-cores default measurably slows these down (thread sync overhead per op exceeds the compute saved on small batches/models) -- 4 was found empirically faster than both 1 and os.cpu_count(). Re-benchmark if the model or batch size changes materially.
ppo._comment_dir_log_std_reg: Explicit L2 restoring force pulling move_dir_log_std toward dir_log_std_target and kick_dir_log_std toward kick_dir_log_std_target. move_* keys fall back to dir_log_std_* for backward compat. Without this, ent_dir_weight's entropy bonus only ever inflates log_std with nothing pulling it back. 0.0 = disabled. Try 0.01-0.1.
ppo._comment_ent_dir_weight: Weight applied to continuous direction heads (move_dir, kick_dir) in the entropy bonus. The direction heads output a Gaussian distribution; their raw entropy is much larger in scale than a Bernoulli head. 1.0 = equal weight = direction entropy dominates the bonus and the Bernoulli heads (shoot, sprint etc.) get almost no exploration pressure. 0.05 = direction entropy contributes only 5% — Bernoulli heads drive exploration. Lower toward 0.01 if the agent spins randomly (too much directional noise); raise toward 0.2 if kicks/passes cluster on one angle.
ppo._comment_augment: Slot permutations per geometric flip variant. Total batch multiplier = 4 * n. Use 1 for 4x (flips only), 3 for 12x, 0 to disable. See ai/obs/augment.py.
ppo._comment_rollout_eval: Number of trials run vs rules-based AI after each PPO rollout update. Set to 0 to disable the per-rollout eval entirely.
ppo._comment: Standard PPO defaults from CleanRL-style reference implementations. Tune empirically.

curriculum._comment_todo: TODO: implement and wire up: rng_reduction_start/end (randomisation annealing over training), pitch_standard_fraction (fraction of episodes on standard pitch), pitch_min_scale / goal_min_scale (curriculum pitch scaling). Currently not read by any code.
curriculum._comment_phase1_opponent: phase1 training opponent split expressed as unnormalized ratios (normalized at read time). Neural remainder is used during PPO training as a secondary player. During demo recording, neural falls back to Phase1RulesAI — no neural opponent exists at demo time. Immobile-opponent episodes are excluded from BC training by DemonstrationDataset.valid_indices().
curriculum._comment_secondary_weight: Importance weight applied to secondary (opponent) player transitions in the PPO loss. 1.0 = equal weight, 0.5 = half weight, 0.0 = ignore secondary transitions.

bc._comment: Behavioural cloning from rules-based AI. Set pretrain_steps=0 to skip pre-training. Set aux_coeff_start=0.0 to disable the PPO auxiliary BC loss.
bc._comment_label_smoothing: Label smoothing for BC Bernoulli targets before BCE: target = target*(1-eps) + 0.5*eps. dec_label_smoothing applies to the 7 decision heads (shoot/pass/move/tackle/gp_extra/mark/hold); exec_label_smoothing applies to the 4 execution Bernoulli heads (exec_move, sprint, kick_this_tick, tackle_attempt). 0.0 = disabled (default). Try 0.02-0.05 if BC-primed heads become overconfident and cause PPO's per-minibatch KL early-stop to fire on minibatch 0 of the first rollout (see ai_trainer_knowledge.md / training log analysis) — exec_move/sprint sitting at confident post-BC probabilities makes Bernoulli KL highly nonlinear, so even a tiny first gradient step overshoots target_kl.
bc._comment_pos_weight: null = auto-compute from the training dataset at load time via DemonstrationDataset.compute_pos_weights() (recommended). Set a float to override. pos_weight_max caps the auto-computed inverse-frequency ratio (e.g. tackle_attempt was hitting ~134.5) before use — null = uncapped. Only applies to the auto-computed path; has no effect when pos_weight_kick/pos_weight_tackle_attempt are set explicitly.
bc._comment_max_grad_norm: Grad-norm clip for BC pretrain's optimizers (Phase 0 demo_opt, Phase 1 bc_opt, Phase 4 repair_opt). Absent from config = fall back to ppo.max_grad_norm (prior behaviour, shares PPO's very conservative clip). Set a float here to give BC pretrain its own cap instead -- BC uses a much higher LR (bc_learning_rate) and full supervised minibatch descent with no PPO trust-region concept, so PPO's tight clip can suppress useful large early-training corrections. Set explicitly to null (as here) to disable clipping entirely during BC.
bc._comment_downsample: Gentle per-epoch downsampling of 'trivial' BC movement rows (see DemonstrationDataset._compute_trivial_mask). frac_default is used for epochs < epoch_threshold, frac_high_epoch afterward. Freshly re-rolled every epoch, never a fixed one-time filter.
bc._comment_aux: aux_coeff anneals linearly from start to end over aux_coeff_anneal_fraction of training (e.g. 0.3 = done by 30% of steps). The BC loss is computed on decision Bernoulli heads and execution move_direction.
bc._comment_bc_pretrain_early_stop: Episode-level 85/15 train/val split + early stop for pretrain_combined()'s main BC epoch loop, mirroring value_pretrain_early_stop_patience/min_delta below. patience=0 (default) = disabled (no split computed, no early stop -- matches prior behaviour of training BC blind on the full dataset for exactly bc_pretrain_epochs). Set e.g. 3-5 to enable: patience = consecutive non-improving epochs allowed before stopping and restoring best-val weights; min_delta = minimum val BC-loss decrease to count as improvement. See 'BC val=' log line when enabled.
bc._comment_dec_exec_weight: Relative weight of decision-network vs execution-network losses in BC (pretrain and PPO aux annealing). dec=1.0/exec=1.0 = equal. Raise bc_exec_weight to push execution network (sprint, direction, tackle) harder; lower to let it drift more freely under RL.
bc._comment_combined_pretrain_rollout_steps: Steps to collect for the on-policy rollout used by pretrain_combined()'s joint BC + value warm-up (its rollout_steps= argument) when an offline --bc-dataset is supplied. Completely separate variable from value_pretrain_steps below (the standalone pretrain_value() fallback used when no dataset is given) — the two are never meant to share a value, tune independently. Also independent of ppo.rollout_steps (the main PPO rollout buffer size).
bc._comment_value_pretrain_batch_size: Minibatch size for pretrain_value()'s value-only fitting loop (and Phase 0's demo-return value warm-up inside pretrain_combined()). Previously fell back silently to ppo.minibatch_size (12000) -- that size is tuned for PPO's clip/KL-early-stop dynamics, not for a plain supervised value-MSE regression, so it was an accidental coupling rather than a deliberate one. 512 gives noisier-but-more-frequent gradient steps, generally better for this kind of regression. Tune independently of ppo.minibatch_size and bc.bc_pretrain_batch_size.
bc._comment_value_pretrain_weight_decay: Adam weight_decay (L2) applied to pretrain_value()'s value optimizer(s) (execution_net.value_head-only optimizer, or trainer.value_net's optimizer when --separate-value-net). 0.0 (default) = disabled, matching prior behaviour. Motivated by train loss falling steadily (e.g. 0.41->0.30) while val loss RISES (0.46->0.57) over ~17 epochs before early-stop -- classic overfitting to a small, autocorrelated offline rollout reused for many epochs. Try 1e-4 to 1e-3; complements value_dropout (network.value_dropout) and the early-stop patience/min_delta below.
bc._comment_value_pretrain_early_stop: Value-pretrain-only early stop (see 'Value epoch' log lines): patience = consecutive non-improving epochs allowed before stopping; min_delta = minimum val-loss decrease to count as improvement. Raise patience if val loss looks noisy but still trending down slowly; raise min_delta to stop sooner on marginal improvements.
bc._comment_bc_value_coef: Weight of the value MSE term added to the full BC pre-train loss in Phase 1 (both networks, demo returns). Separate from phase0_value_coef (decision-net-only Phase 0 warm-up). Falls back to demo_value_bc_coef if absent for backward compatibility.
bc._comment_phase0_value_coef: Weight of the value MSE term added to the decision-heads-only BC loss in Phase 0 (demo value pretrain). Phase 0 trains decision_net only (not execution_net), with NO frozen layers (unlike pretrain_value()'s standalone freezing) - one combined backward pass per minibatch: decision_bc_loss + phase0_value_coef * value_loss.
bc._comment_bc_only_continuation_epochs: Epoch budget for a BC-only continuation loop in PPOTrainer._ppo_update() that runs AFTER the value-only continuation (see ppo.value_only_continuation_epochs), when the policy's per-minibatch KL early-stop (ppo.target_kl) cuts the main epoch loop short. Runs bc_loss_from_tensor() + optimizer.step() on decision_net/execution_net params ONLY — no policy forward pass, no ratio/KL computed, so it cannot itself trigger further early-stops — using bc_only_continuation_coeff if set, otherwise falling back to the SAME annealed bc_coeff already computed for this rollout (see aux_coeff_start/end/anneal_fraction above). Rationale: BC's aux loss is normally applied inside the same KL-gated epoch/minibatch loop as the policy loss, so frequent early-stops were silently truncating BC's intended gradient budget every rollout (the value head already got its own dedicated continuation, BC did not). Default 0 = disabled (opt-in, new/experimental) — try 2-6 if BC influence looks weaker than aux_coeff implies (frequent early-stops + BC still not converging). Set 0 to disable without affecting the value-only continuation.
bc._comment_bc_only_continuation_coeff: Optional fixed coefficient for the bc-only continuation loop, decoupled from the annealed aux_coeff used by the in-epoch BC aux loss. null (default) = fall back to the annealed bc_coeff (prior behaviour) — this means setting aux_coeff_start/end to anneal to 0.0 also silently zeroes this continuation's effect even if bc_only_continuation_epochs > 0. Set a float (e.g. 0.3) to keep this continuation loop contributing a fixed BC gradient even after aux_coeff has annealed to 0, so BC no longer fights the main policy gradient during the KL-gated epoch loop but still nudges decision_net/execution_net toward demo behaviour using otherwise-unused post-early-stop gradient budget.
bc._comment_from_ckpt: These _from_ckpt variants are used instead of the defaults when --pretrain-from-checkpoint or --latest-pretrain is passed. Typically fewer epochs and lower aux coefficients since the policy is already near the demonstrations.
bc._comment_frozen_layers: Layers frozen (requires_grad=False) during value head warm-up. -1=all non-value layers (encoders + full trunk). 0=nothing frozen (gradients flow freely through trunk). 1=encoders only. 2=encoders + trunk layer 1. 3=encoders + full trunk (same as -1). Default -1 matches prior behaviour.
bc._comment_value: After BC pre-training, run value-only MSE warm-up so the critic is near the true return scale before PPO starts. Used by the standalone pretrain_value() fallback path (no --bc-dataset). value_pretrain_steps is independent of ppo.rollout_steps — 32768 ≈ 4× rollout buffer (~700 episodes). See ppo.combined_pretrain_rollout_steps for the equivalent sizing when pretrain_combined() is used instead. 15% of episodes held out as a val set; epoch loop stops early if val loss stagnates for 5 consecutive epochs. Set value_pretrain_steps=0 to skip.
bc._comment_demo_sample: Time between timed observation samples during demonstration recording. Kick2 and tackles are always recorded regardless.
bc._comment_demo_recording_n_processes: Number of worker PROCESSES for record_demonstrations.py (--n-processes overrides this). 1 (default) = current single-process behaviour. >1 splits --n-episodes evenly across that many subprocesses, each independently driving rules-based AI on both sides (no policy network, no weight sync needed -- much simpler than ppo.n_parallel_envs) and writing its own disjoint range of phase{N}_XXXX.npz files. Same GIL/physics rationale as ppo.n_parallel_envs -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Parallel rollout collection'.

ema._comment: EMA smoothing for attack/defence weighting (section 2.7). alpha close to 1 = slow change, further from 1 = fast change.

phase1._comment_dist_shaping: Legacy positional retreat penalty (metres retreated × coef). Set to 0.0 to use heading_penalty_coef instead (recommended). Falls back to ball_distance_shaping if keys absent.
phase1._comment_ball_approach_speed_bonus: Squared closing-speed bonus: coef * max(0, prev_ball_dist - curr_ball_dist)^2 per step (0.0 disables). ball_approach_bonus/ball_retreat_penalty above are LINEAR in the per-step distance delta, which is potential-based and telescopes over an episode to coef*(start_dist-end_dist) — a player closing 10m in 2 fast steps and one closing the same 10m in 20 slow steps earn IDENTICAL total reward from those terms, so they cannot reward speed, only final position. Squaring breaks the telescoping (sum(x_i^2) >= (sum(x_i))^2/n, equality only when every step closes the same amount), so concentrating the same net distance into fewer/faster steps yields strictly more reward. Tune independently of ball_approach_bonus — a sensible starting point is roughly 2-5x ball_approach_bonus since per-step deltas are typically < 1.0m (squaring shrinks small values). See 'appr_sq' in the reward breakdown/training log.
phase1._comment_ball_retreat_speed_penalty: Squared retreating-speed penalty: coef * max(0, curr_ball_dist - prev_ball_dist)^2 per step, the symmetric-but-asymmetric-coefficient partner to ball_approach_speed_bonus (mirrors the existing ball_retreat_penalty > ball_approach_bonus asymmetry above). Falls back to ball_approach_speed_bonus's value if absent. Set higher than ball_approach_speed_bonus to penalize fast retreating more than fast approaching is rewarded. _delta = prev_ball_dist - curr_ball_dist is already the ball-relative closing speed (distance closed this step, i.e. player speed projected onto the direction to the ball) — not raw player speed — so this term only ever fires on genuine retreat along the ball axis.
phase1._comment_ball_approach_speed_reward_clam: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE positive ('approach') side of 'appr_sq' (via reward.cumulative_clamped_delta(), not a per-step clamp), same rationale as ball_progress_reward_clamp but applied to appr_sq instead of prog. null = uncapped default.
phase1._comment_ball_retreat_speed_reward_clamp: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE negative ('retreat') side of 'appr_sq' independently of ball_approach_speed_reward_clamp above — deliberately a SEPARATE bound (not one symmetric clamp) so it can match the already-independent ball_approach_speed_bonus/ball_retreat_speed_penalty coefficient asymmetry. null = uncapped default.
phase1._comment_heading_penalty: Penalty for moving away from the ball based on velocity direction vs ball direction. Formula: -coef * max(0, 1 - cos_sim)^exp. Only fires when |velocity| > min_speed_mps. cos_sim=1 (toward ball)=0 penalty; cos_sim=0 (perpendicular)=-coef; cos_sim=-1 (away)=-coef*2^exp. Set coef=0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_stamina_penalty: End-of-episode penalty for stamina level: -coef * (1 - final_stamina). Range [0, coef]: 0 when full stamina, coef when completely exhausted. Applied once at episode termination only. Set to 0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_ball_progress_reward_clamp: Caps the EPISODE-CUMULATIVE 'prog' total (via reward.cumulative_clamped_delta(), not a per-step clamp) so a long/wandering possession episode can't sum |prog| far past this value one small step at a time. null = uncapped.
phase1._comment_loss_terminal: Penalty applied when the opponent reaches the trainee's box with possession (trainee loses). Should be negative and less than box_possession_terminal in magnitude.
phase1._comment_loss_of_possession: Small penalty per step the trainee loses the ball to the opponent. Creates symmetric signal with gain_possession_bonus.
phase1._comment_timeout_penalty: Penalty if the episode times out (no resolution). Makes timeouts clearly worse than active play.
phase1._comment_proximity_bonus: On timeout only: bonus for how close the ball was to the opponent box. scale * max(0, 1 - dist/30m). Max = scale at box edge. Rewards making progress even when not winning.
phase1._comment_step_penalty: Flat penalty applied every decision step (including terminal). Encourages finishing quickly independent of episode outcome. Total episode cost = step_penalty * n_steps; with a 50s episode at 0.3s intervals that's ~167 steps, so step_penalty=0.01 costs ~1.67 over a full episode. Set to 0.0 to disable.
phase1._comment_speed_bonus: Bonus for finishing fast: scale * time_remaining_fraction. Max = scale (instant finish). Set to 0.0 to disable.

phase1_scenario._comment_opponent_dist: Constrain opponent placement distance from trainee. Both default to unconstrained. E.g. min=5, max=20 keeps opponent nearby but not on top.
